card.name: Comma after Sodium Chloride Injection
card.fires_on: The comma right after a diluent name such as 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection or 5% Dextrose Injection, just before USP, in dilution and reconstitution instructions.

modes.label: Comma before USP
modes.description: A comma following a named IV diluent, where USP comes next.
modes.example: ELZONRIS: One infusion syringe pump One empty 10 mL sterile vial 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection<<,>> USP Three 10 mL sterile

modes.label: Stray linking words
modes.description: Occasional weaker hits on small words in instructions, such as only or the.
modes.example: ONCASPAR does not contain a preservative. Use<< only>> one dose per vial; discard unused

card.writes: No clear link to the promoted tokens, which are a scattered mix of mostly non-English words and the words suspension and cotton.
card.plain: It fires on the comma after the name of a dilution fluid like saline or dextrose in mixing directions.
